notes: Step 1 parts were right, so I kept them unchanged. The UNO WiFi Rev2 is not in the catalogue and lookup_part found nothing, so it stays a new part type with Uno-style header pins.
Circuit as drawn: pin 2, green wire, resistor (220 ohm), LED anode; LED cathode, black wire, GND. The sketch drives the LED from pin 2, so the circuit matches the text.

Breadboard coordinates are read from the image. Its labelled rows f-j are on the top half, which the catalogue calls bank 'b', so I used 'b' hole names. The green wire is in column 3 row g, the resistor spans column 3 to column 6 on row h, the LED legs are in column 6 (anode, bent leg) and column 8 (cathode) on row i, and the black wire is in column 8 row h.
The resistor sits on the LED's anode side, as in the image. The black wire goes to the GND pin next to AREF, which I called GND.1. The three GND pins are the same node.
The built-in LED is an alternative the tutorial mentions, but the image uses the external LED, so I did not build it. A1 is read in software with nothing connected, so it has no wiring.
